new_content.title: Linear equations with x on both sides
new_content.intro: You already know how to get x alone when it sits on one side of the equals sign. Now x shows up on BOTH sides, like 3x + 5 = x + 17. The fix is one new move at the start: gather all the x terms on one side first, then solve the way you already know.

sections.heading: The new rule: collect the x terms first
sections.body: When x appears on both sides, subtract the smaller x term from BOTH sides before doing anything else. Subtracting the smaller one keeps the x term positive, which avoids sign trouble. After that, the equation is just a one-sided equation you already know how to solve.
sections.example: 3x + 5 = x + 17. The x terms are 3x and x. Subtract x from both sides: 3x - x + 5 = x - x + 17, which gives 2x + 5 = 17. The x terms now live on one side only.

sections.heading: Then finish the way you already know
sections.body: Once the x terms are together, undo the constant with addition or subtraction, then undo the multiplication with division. Do those on both sides, in that order.
sections.example: From 2x + 5 = 17, subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 12. Then divide both sides by 2: x = 6. That is the solution.

sections.heading: Check by substituting
sections.body: Put your answer into BOTH original sides and see if they match. This catches every sign slip you can make along the way, so never skip it.
sections.example: With x = 6 in 3x + 5 = x + 17: the left side is 3(6) + 5 = 18 + 5 = 23. The right side is 6 + 17 = 23. Both sides are 23, so x = 6 is correct.

steps: Name the x terms: 7x on the left, 3x on the right. Subtract the smaller one, 3x, from both sides.
7x - 3x - 2 = 3x - 3x + 18 gives 4x - 2 = 18. The x terms are now all on the left.
Undo the -2 by adding 2 to both sides: 4x - 2 + 2 = 18 + 2, so 4x = 20.
Undo the multiplication by 4 by dividing both sides by 4: x = 20 / 4 = 5.
Check by substituting x = 5. Left: 7(5) - 2 = 35 - 2 = 33. Right: 3(5) + 18 = 15 + 18 = 33. Both sides are 33, so x = 5 is correct.

common_mistakes: Subtracting the x term from one side only. In 3x + 5 = x + 17, subtracting x from just the left gives 2x + 5 = x + 17 while the right still has x, so the two sides are no longer equal and every later step is wrong.

Dropping the constant after collecting x terms. In 3x + 5 = x + 17, subtracting x gives 2x + 5 = 17; forgetting the +5 and writing 2x = 17 leads to x = 17/2, which fails the check (3(17/2)+5 is not 17/2 + 17).
Subtracting the larger x term and then losing a negative sign. In 2x + 9 = 5x - 3, subtracting 5x gives -3x + 9 = -3, then -3x = -12. Dividing gives x = 4, not x = -4. Both negatives cancel.
Collecting x terms and then dividing before removing the constant. From 2x + 5 = 17, dividing by 2 first gives x + 5/2 = 17/2 and a wrong answer; subtract 5 first.
new_content.summary: When x is on both sides, subtract the smaller x term from both sides first to collect the x terms on one side. Then subtract or add to clear the constant, then divide. Check by substituting your answer into both original sides.

check_questions.prompt: In 4x + 3 = x + 15, which first step leaves x on only one side?
check_questions.rationale: Subtracting x from both sides gives 3x + 3 = 15, so x is on only one side. Subtracting 3 from both sides gives 4x = x + 12, which still has x on both sides.
Subtract 3x from both sides to get 4x - 2 = 18, add 2 to get 4x = 20, then divide by 4 to get x = 5.

check_questions.prompt: After subtracting 3x from both sides of 3x + 8 = 7x - 4, what equation do you have?
check_questions.rationale: The left becomes 3x - 3x + 8 = 8, and the right becomes 7x - 3x - 4 = 4x - 4. The constant -4 is not affected by subtracting 3x.
Subtract 2x from both sides to get 10 = 3x - 8, add 8 to get 18 = 3x, then divide by 3 to get x = 6. Checking: 2(6) + 10 = 22 and 5(6) - 8 = 22.
